meetings.headline: Town meeting narrowly passed sweeping town-employee benefit/hiring changes over a select board member's objection.
meetings.summary: This was Lunenburg's fall 2024 special town meeting, covering fifteen warrant articles: budget transfers, an elderly tax exemption COLA, a rewritten water supply protection bylaw, several revolving funds, a request to explore selling or leasing the Brooks House, and two lengthy, contested articles amending the town's salary administration plan to add sick banks, holiday pay, merit awards and employment contracts aimed at staff recruitment and retention. minutes.headline: Town meeting narrowly passed sweeping town-employee benefit/hiring changes over a select board member's objection.
minutes.summary: This was Lunenburg's fall 2024 special town meeting, covering fifteen warrant articles: budget transfers, an elderly tax exemption COLA, a rewritten water supply protection bylaw, several revolving funds, a request to explore selling or leasing the Brooks House, and two lengthy, contested articles amending the town's salary administration plan to add sick banks, holiday pay, merit awards and employment contracts aimed at staff recruitment and retention. The salary plan articles drew extended public debate over the lack of a seated Personnel Committee and process speed but passed; a Marshall Park renovation appropriation and a citizen petition article were both passed over without action.

what_happened.line: Voters passed sweeping changes to town-employee pay and benefits, despite objections over the empty Personnel Committee seat.
A rewrite of the water supply protection bylaw passed, after residents raised concerns about lake water withdrawal and which map applied.
Voters asked the select board to study selling or leasing the Brooks House, without authorizing any sale.
A Marshall Park renovation appropriation was passed over after cost estimates came in far higher than expected.
Voters approved additional funds for the FY25 school operating budget and for current-year salary and health insurance lines.

why_it_matters: The salary plan changes touch pay, sick time, holidays and hiring contracts for every town employee, and were adopted without a seated Personnel Committee to vet them.
The water bylaw rewrite governs protections around the town's water supply and the lakes near Hickory Hills, an area several residents spoke about directly.
Residents should expect a revised Marshall Park proposal at spring town meeting, and a select-board report on the Brooks House's future.

Select board report on selling or leasing the Brooks House

meetings.headline: Town meeting passed the FY26 school and town budget with deep staff cuts and voted on a $948,000 school override.
meetings.summary: Annual Town Meeting worked through the full warrant: consent-calendar articles, a Wetlands revolving fund, prior-year bills, reserve-fund transfers, a contested capital plan, the $44M-plus Omnibus budget (which includes deep school staffing cuts as one-time ESSER and ARPA funds expire), a $948,000 Proposition 2½ override for the schools that still needs town-election approval, salary and leave-policy changes for non-union employees, the sewer enterprise budget, a cemetery-lots appropriation, a lowered senior property-tax exemption age, re-adoption of the OPEB trust statute, a historical commission bylaw codification, and a new battery-storage/solar zoning bylaw. Numerous floor amendments were proposed on the capital plan, the cemetery appropriation, and the parental-leave article, with mixed results, and the override's final town-meeting vote tally was not clearly announced in the captions.

what_happened.line: Town meeting approved the town/school Omnibus budget 309-37, which includes deep school staffing cuts as one-time COVID relief funds run out.
Town meeting also acted on a Proposition 2½ override for the schools, an amount heard as roughly an amount as heard but the final tally was not clearly announced in the recording.
The override still needs separate approval at a town election before it can take effect.
The FY25 capital plan passed 320-31 after floor amendments to cut Turkey Hill safety-film and Wallace Park court funding both failed.
Town meeting changed the parental sick-leave policy for non-union employees, passing it as amended 123-13.

why_it_matters: The Omnibus budget sets what schools and town departments can spend this year, and the staffing cuts tied to it follow the expiration of temporary federal pandemic aid, not a new decision to cut on its own.
The override next goes to a town-election ballot; if approved there, it would raise the tax levy above the state's normal cap specifically to fund schools.
The capital plan funds building and site work, including two disputed projects, at Turkey Hill and Wallace Park, that residents will see this year.
